Q156.L1t: The Edinburgh Fringe is a large arts event that takes place in Scotland's capital each August.
Q156.L2t: The Fringe began in 1947, when eight theatre groups arrived uninvited and performed in a pub that had been disused for years.
Q156.L3t: The passage says that after the first uninvited troupes, groups from Edinburgh, Oxford, Cambridge, Durham and Birmingham universities travelled to the city every summer to stage little-known plays in small church halls.
Q156.L4t: The people who joined the Fringe after it appeared were groups of students from universities.
Q156.L2f: The Fringe was first held in 1959, when nineteen theatre groups performed in the city's official festival venues.
Q156.L3f: The passage says that the groups who arrived after the first troupes were mainly professional musicians and dancers who came to fill the stages of the Fringe.
Q156.L4f: The people who came to join the Fringe after it appeared were musicians and dancers.

Q157.L1t: Smoking is one of the leading preventable causes of illness and early death around the world.
Q157.L2t: The research team analysed questionnaires from just under 35,000 people, focusing on 4,800 daily smokers who were interviewed twice, three years apart.
Q157.L3t: The professor explicitly admits that the team cannot tell whether better mental health comes first or quitting causes it, and she describes only a strong link between the two.
Q157.L4t: She agrees only that quitting smoking and better mental health are strongly associated, without claiming that one causes the other.
Q157.L2f: The survey used in the study questioned each participant only once, during the 1990s, so no follow-up interviews were done.
Q157.L3f: The professor states that her data prove stopping smoking directly causes psychiatric problems to improve, with mental health never being the starting point.
Q157.L4f: She agrees that giving up cigarettes is what brings about a better psychiatric outlook.

Q158.L1t: Deserts are very dry regions found on several continents, and they cover a large share of the Earth's land.
Q158.L2t: The passage describes desert sand and rocks as hard, and says many desert plants have hard needles in place of leaves.
Q158.L3t: The passage mentions desert plants with needles instead of leaves, so it shows that living things do exist in these dry lands.
Q158.L4t: The claim that deserts contain no living things is the false statement.
Q158.L2f: The passage says Iran stops desert growth by spraying a thin layer of water over the sand and then planting grass.
Q158.L3f: The passage says that in the last 100 years deserts have changed only very slowly, because their growth is caused by natural processes that take millions of years.
Q158.L4f: The claim that deserts have been growing quickly is the statement that is not true.
